issues: Overall Time Below Range (TBR) is elevated at 5.1%, with severe clustering overnight (18.5% at 00:00, 10.1% at 01:00) and in the early evening (15.3% at 18:00).
The 90 mg/dL glucose target overnight provides insufficient buffer against hypoglycemia while Unannounced Meal (UAM) and Dynamic ISF are active.
System safety limits are dangerously loose; a max basal of 12 U/h allows the pump to deliver nearly 18 to 20 times the scheduled basal rate of 0.6 U/h during a UAM spike.

Zero carbohydrates are logged, meaning 100% reliance on UAM logic. Combined with GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying, insulin is front-loaded reactively and outpaces food absorption, causing late-stage crashes.
summary: Glucose control shows an excellent 86.0% Time in Range, but at the cost of significant hypoglycemia. The user is managing meals entirely without logging carbohydrates (UAM-only). Because GLP-1 therapy slows digestion, the reactive UAM SMBs stack insulin too quickly, leading to severe late-meal and overnight lows. The risk is compounded by extremely high AAPS safety limits and a tight 90 mg/dL overnight target.
education: GLP-1 medications significantly delay stomach emptying. When meals digest slowly, insulin needs to be stretched out over a longer period.
Unannounced Meal (UAM) logic detects rising glucose and assumes a standard meal curve. It front-loads insulin to stop the spike.
When UAM front-loads insulin for a delayed GLP-1 meal, the insulin peaks before the food does, creating a 'mismatch' crash hours later.
Max Basal (U/h) acts as the ultimate safety cap on SMBs. A limit of 12 U/h on a 0.6 U/h profile allows massive, rapid insulin stacking.
strengths: High Time in Range (86.0%) despite complex meal dynamics.
Excellent sensor data coverage (98.7%) with consistent loop execution.
Strong baseline stability when UAM and SMB are inactive.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Severe lows reaching 41-42 mg/dL have been recorded. Addressing the max basal limits and overnight targets should be prioritized immediately.

analysis_steps.findings: Excellent CGM coverage at 98.7% over 14 days with robust loop telemetry. However, exactly zero carbohydrates are logged, meaning all meal management is unannounced.
analysis_steps.evidence: Total carbs 0.0g, carb_entries 0. 3995 CGM entries with only 10 gaps.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The lack of logged carbs prevents direct evaluation of Carb Ratios (CR) and conventional meal bolus timing.

analysis_steps.findings: Significant hypoglycemia risk is present. Overall TBR is 5.1%, peaking dramatically between 23:00-03:00 and 18:00-19:00. Minimum recorded glucose is 41 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: TBR is 18.5% at hour 0, 15.3% at hour 18, and 10.1% at hour 22. Glucose extremes list multiple events in the 40s.

analysis_steps.findings: Basal rates (0.5-0.8 U/h) are reasonable, but the overnight target of 90 mg/dL is too aggressive. It leaves no safety buffer against UAM or Dynamic ISF overshoot.
analysis_steps.evidence: Target segments map to 90 mg/dL at 23:00 and 00:00, aligning exactly with the hours of highest TBR.

analysis_steps.findings: The 10-hour DIA is conservative. The flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U is an anchor, but CR is entirely unused. Heavy late-action drops are visible after small correction doses.
analysis_steps.evidence: Therapy response windows show drops up to 178 mg/dL following minor correction boluses under 0.65U. CR settings exist but are functionally bypassed.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: True CR effectiveness cannot be observed without logged carbohydrates.

analysis_steps.findings: The system is relying 100% on UAM to manage food. Safety limits are dangerously permissive; max_basal is 12 U/h and max_IOB is 25 U, allowing the loop to deliver massive SMBs for unannounced spikes.
analysis_steps.evidence: AAPS loop statuses frequently cite 'UAM Boost' and 'SMB equals...'. max_basal_u_per_hour is 12.0.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF is enabled at 70% and aggressively sharpens the ISF during UAM spikes (down to ~36 mg/dL/U). This compounds with the high max basal limit to cause insulin stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: Loop status shows Dosing sensitivity swinging wildly based on BG momentum. Autosens is disabled but Dynamic ISF overrides this.

analysis_steps.findings: The user applies a completely reactive strategy with no prebolus, no immediate bolus, and no carb logging. The system is forced to guess meal sizes from BG changes.
analysis_steps.evidence: 0 carb entries, 0 preboluses. Total reliance on UAM logic.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: User's actual meal timing and sizing are undocumented.

analysis_steps.findings: Despite GLP-1 usage heavily delaying digestion, no extended carbs (e-carbs) are used. The mismatch between fast reactive UAM insulin and slow GLP-1 digestion drives the severe late lows.

The severe overnight and evening lows are caused by a combination of UAM stacking insulin for slow-digesting (GLP-1) meals, enabled by overly loose safety limits and a tight overnight target. Safety limits and targets must be adjusted first.
analysis_steps.evidence: Combining the 12 U/h max basal, 100% UAM usage, GLP-1 notes, and 90 mg/dL target perfectly models the observed 5.1% TBR pattern.

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Target to Build Safety Buffer
recommendations.description: A target of 90 mg/dL leaves no room for error when UAM overshoots. Raising the 23:00 target to at least 110 mg/dL will command the loop to suspend insulin earlier before hypoglycemia occurs.

recommendations.title: Reduce Max Basal and Max IOB Limits
recommendations.description: The current max basal of 12 U/h allows the system to deliver nearly 20x the scheduled basal rate during UAM spikes. Capping this at roughly 3-4x average basal (~3 U/h) and max IOB to ~8 U will safely throttle insulin stacking.

recommendations.title: Utilize E-Carbs for GLP-1 Digestion
recommendations.description: Because GLP-1 slows digestion, reactive UAM delivers insulin too fast. Logging meals using extended carbs (e-carbs) instead of relying entirely on UAM will stretch insulin delivery to match the food absorption.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise the 23:00 and 00:00 targets from 90 mg/dL to 110 mg/dL to create a larger safety buffer against overnight lows.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Extremely permissive limits allow UAM to stack massive amounts of insulin for slow-digesting meals. Throttling max basal to ~4x standard basal prevents severe overshoot.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user relies entirely on Unannounced Meals (UAM) without logging carbs. Because GLP-1 delays digestion, UAM front-loads insulin too quickly based on early glucose spikes, leading to a severe insulin/food mismatch and late-stage crashes.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Transition to logging meals using extended carbs (e-carbs) to instruct the loop to stretch insulin delivery, matching the delayed GLP-1 absorption curve.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Monitor late-evening and overnight Time Below Range after applying e-carbs and throttling max basal limits.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Increase the 23:00 and 00:00 profile targets from 90 mg/dL to 110 mg/dL to provide a safer buffer against overnight lows.
Step 2: Reduce AAPS safety limits drastically (e.g., max_basal_u_per_hour to 3 U/h and max_iob_units to 8 U) to prevent UAM from stacking extreme amounts of insulin.
Step 3: Begin testing e-carbs (extended carbs) for meals instead of relying 100% on UAM, which will help stretch insulin delivery to match the slow digestion caused by GLP-1.
